lines.text: Too bright.
Turn that shit down.
Black. Obviously.
That black does not match the other black and I hate that I can tell.
Purple light. Better.
No beige. We have standards.
I was dressing like this before half the internet learned the word goth.
Needs more silver.
That outfit needs one unnecessary dramatic thing.
Yes, I own another black coat.
Nighttime is the correct lighting.
I don't want cute spooky. I want old haunted building.
The lipstick is staying dark.
I like elegant with a little threat.
Somehow the boots are still not dramatic enough.
I want the room to look like midnight pays rent here.
Anything can be improved by making it darker and adding one tiny glow.
I've never regretted buying something that looked mildly vampiric.
The correct amount of lace is determined after adding more lace.
My wardrobe is mostly different dialects of black.
If it catches moonlight dramatically, I probably want it.
I respect beige as a warning label.
This corner needs more haunted-library energy.
I want fancy, feral, and vaguely immortal.
The necklace isn't excessive. Your baseline is timid.
I've a professional relationship with dramatic silhouettes.
Someone invented bright cheerful decor and I took that personally.
I'm not hiding in the shadows. The shadows have better ambience.
There's an important distinction between messy and cursed.
This outfit says I've opinions about cemetery architecture.
I could wear a normal coat, but where is the narrative?
My aesthetic goal is still elegant cryptid with good posture.
The black nail polish is doing emotional support work.
Velvet has never betrayed me.
This light is too white. It knows what it did.
Give me candlelight without the house-fire subplot.
The room should look inviting to exactly the right weird people.
I want the background to whisper something ancient has Bluetooth.
The line between goth and expensive widow is beautifully thin.
I dressed for a meeting with a vampire who respects tailoring.
I need one absurd ring to finish the argument.
There should be a legal minimum amount of mood lighting.
I'm suspicious of any shoe that doesn't announce itself.
A good outfit should feel like armor that learned manners.
If the mirror says dramatic, the mirror is finally being useful.
I prefer my elegance with visible teeth.
The furniture could stand to look more like it has secrets.
Soft purple light makes everything look ten percent more supernatural.
I'm not overdressed. Reality is underproduced.
My favorite accessory is still looking like I know a forbidden archive.
